training.device_name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition
training.note: --seed drives the numpy split permutation and torch parameter init. Re-running this command on a CUDA device regenerates theta, scale, bias and every metric bit for bit: five consecutive runs of each Round 47 artifact, and two independent runs of each Round 84 one (for medical and telecom the pre-registered experiment and the retrain, for finance the four-column retrain and a repeat of it), max |diff| 0. That is true only since the multiclass readout stopped using index_add_, whose CUDA atomicAdd made the same seeded command land on macro F1 0.809846 or 0.807781 depending on the run. On a CPU it is not guaranteed: CPU and CUDA kernels differ in float rounding, and a long multiclass run amplifies that.

note: Variational QCNN trained by backpropagation through a dense state vector. The prediction path applies NO QOTP mask: undoing a Pauli frame through Clifford+T is not implemented here (T X T-dagger is not Pauli), so hiding and prediction are kept separate rather than claiming a correction that does not exist. Simulated, not hardware; the classical baseline above is reported so no quantum advantage is implied.

circuit.name: tree
circuit.bonds: the disjoint pairs (0,1), (2,3), ... of the active register only
circuit.block: 8 shared angles per round: RY and RZ on each wire, CNOT(a, b), then RZ and RY on each wire
circuit.pooling: CRY from the discarded wire onto its kept partner, 1 shared angle per stage; an odd register's last wire is pooled into the first
circuit.simulability: a tree of two-qubit blocks: after every pooling stage the survivors are a product of one-qubit states, so it is classically simulable in linear time at any width
